deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1983-84 study of systems of pseudo-lines, that is, arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane. The plane is drawn in the disc (here half-disc) model: the boundary circle stands for the line at infinity, with antipodal points identified. Every drawing on this page is such a half-disc. Its boundary arc is coded by colour:
- dark-brown thick segments;
- yellow-green segments;
- green dots marking endpoints or transition points.

Left column, three figures. These show a bundle of mutually 'parallel' pseudolines, drawn as red vertical strokes. The bundle leaves the top dark segment of the boundary and descends into the disc. Small red tally marks (=, ≡) on the boundary record how many strands leave through each boundary interval. In the second and third rows one further pseudoline, a long red or pencil diagonal, is drawn crossing the whole bundle. This is the standard configuration for analysing how a single line traverses a parallel class: a 'sweep', or the effect of one line crossing a family. The third-row figure redraws the configuration with the top boundary split into two dark arcs and pencil rays fanning out from a central dot. The middle diagram of row two is a mirror or variant of the left one.

Right-hand side and top-middle, three schematic figures. These replace the drawing by a bookkeeping of signs:
- The top arc of the boundary carries the label +1. The two lateral yellow arcs carry signs ε1 and ε2.
- Inside the disc, a polygonal path joins dots near one end of the boundary to dots near the other.
- In the first figure the path has two segments, labelled ε1 and ε2. The small pencil arrows near the lateral arcs suggest each lateral boundary arc is transported onto the inner segment carrying the same sign.
- In the second figure the inner path has three segments: ε1, −1, ε2.
- In the third it has four: ε1, −1, −1, ε2.

The evident aim is to compare a sign or orientation count along the boundary path (ε1, +1, ε2) with the count along homotopic interior paths. Each new interior segment that replaces part of the top arc contributes −1. This looks like a parity, orientation or local-index computation. In RP², crossing the line at infinity reverses orientation, which is plausibly why the top arc carries +1 while the interior replacements carry −1. It may serve to determine a sign rule for elementary moves (triangle flips) or for the cyclic order of directions at infinity.

The empty pencil circle at upper right is an unused sketch.

The neighbouring pages are consistent with this reading. Page 114 carries combinatorial labels (α0, α1, α2, 1⁺, 1⁻, 3̃, N' = N−1), which suggest an induction on the number N of lines. Page 116 carries quadrilaterals with labelled sides and regions (λ, μ, a, b), i.e. local cell configurations.
errors: No explicit claims are written, so correctness cannot be checked. The sign bookkeeping (+1 on the boundary arc, −1 for each interior replacement segment) is consistent with orientation reversal through the line at infinity in RP², but its exact meaning is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Disc model of RP² with boundary arcs at infinity colour-coded, to study arrangements of pseudolines and bundles of parallel pseudolines
ideas.modern_name: Pseudoline arrangements in the projective plane (Levi, Ringel, Goodman–Pollack); wiring diagrams / allowable sequences
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Levi (1926), G. Ringel (1956), Goodman–Pollack (1980s), Grünbaum
ideas.where_published: Not published by Grothendieck; mentioned only in passing in Récoltes et Semailles as a late interest (unsure of details)

ideas.what: A single pseudoline sweeping across a parallel class of pseudolines, with multiplicities tallied on boundary intervals
ideas.modern_name: Sweeps / allowable sequences; local sequences of an arrangement

ideas.what: Comparing sign or orientation counts along a boundary path versus homotopic interior paths, with each interior segment contributing −1
ideas.modern_name: Orientation character / parity computation in RP²; signs attached to edges of the dual cell complex (cf. chirotope sign changes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (oriented matroid / chirotope theory, Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence 1978)

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds sketches of pseudoline configurations in the disc model and an informal sign bookkeeping along paths. Nothing is stated as a result, and the ideas belong to the standard combinatorics of pseudoline arrangements and oriented matroids. It is of interest only as documentation of Grothendieck's working method.
transcription_corrections: The transcription omits the whole left column and the middle-row figure. These are colour diagrams with no letters: red parallel strokes, a crossing diagonal, red tally marks (=, ≡) on the boundary, and pencil rays.
The top-middle figure has ε1/ε2 labels in three positions on each side: on the outer lateral arc, beside a small pencil arrow sketch, and on the inner segment.
In the second right-hand figure the left inner segment label looks like 'ε1' written over or near '3'. It reads ε1, not a separate symbol.
There is an unlabelled empty pencil circle at upper right.
